memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You will make yourselves unclean by these; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening. Whoever picks up one of their carcasses must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening." - Lev 11:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the chapter turns a corner. It is no longer only about what you eat, but about what you touch — and about what happens next.

Two things stand out. First, uncleanness spreads. It moves from the carcass to the person, and from the person to their clothes. It does not stay where it started. Second, it ends. "Unclean till evening." There is a time limit, a washing, a restoration. This was never a permanent sentence.

Sin behaves like the first half of that. It never stays contained. A private compromise seeps into a marriage. A quiet resentment colours a whole family. A little dishonesty at work spreads until it feels normal. We tell ourselves this one thing will touch nothing else, and we are always wrong (1 Cor 5:6).

But thank God for the second half. Uncleanness had an evening. There was washing, and there was a fresh morning. And in Christ there is something far greater than a ceremonial rinse — there is blood that cleanses us from all sin (1 John 1:7-9), and a God who does not leave us waiting in the dark.

Do not carry today what Christ has already made a way to wash away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you told yourself that a small sin will not spread?
2. Is there something you are still carrying that Christ has already dealt with?
3. What would it look like to come honestly to God for cleansing today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I confess that sin never stays where I leave it. Wash me clean through the blood of Jesus, and let me walk in the freedom of forgiveness rather than in the shadow of what You have already dealt with. Amen.
